task: Build a roadmap for the open-source schema-driven feature flag product (FeatureSync) described in docs/ (notes.md, notes-01.md, notes-02.md, playbooks/). Requirements: production-grade ready; DDD/SOLID/KISS/DRY; fully test-covered; LocalStack used only via environment config through the AWS SDK (no LocalStack-specific code paths).

analysis.objective: Ship @featuresync/core: a local-first, Zod-typed feature flag and configuration runtime that loads a validated immutable snapshot from a local JSON file and evaluates flags in memory with atomic snapshot replacement.
analysis.successDefinition: An application can defineFeature() with a Zod schema, point FEATURESYNC_FILE at a snapshot, and call isEnabled/get/evaluate/version/has/getAll/ready with zero network I/O; invalid snapshots are rejected while the previous one stays active; CI enforces strict TS, lint layer boundaries and 100% line/branch/function/statement coverage.
assumptions: Greenfield repo: only docs/ and docker/docker-compose.yml (LocalStack) exist.
Toolchain: pnpm workspaces, TypeScript strict, Vitest (v8 coverage), ESLint flat config, Node 22 LTS, ESM output via tsup.
Zod is a peer dependency of @featuresync/core; the snapshot JSON contract stays language-neutral so future Python/Go SDKs can consume it.
MVP operators are equals, notEquals, in, and implicit AND across `when` keys; percentage rollout is excluded per docs section 28.
LocalStack is reached only through standard AWS SDK v3 env config (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, AWS_REGION, credentials); no code branches on LocalStack. Applies from horizon 2 onward.
License: Apache-2.0 unless the owner chooses otherwise.
risks: Snapshot JSON contract chosen now becomes a public, cross-language API; a wrong shape forces a breaking version later — include a schemaVersion field from day one.
100% coverage can be gamed with assertion-free tests; rubrics require behavioral assertions, not just execution.
Type-level API (inferring keys and config types from defineFeature) can become complex; keep it to key + config inference only.
Evaluation semantics (rule order, missing attributes, type mismatches) are easy to leave ambiguous and hard to change once published.
outOfScope: S3 snapshot source, SNS listener, periodic reconciliation — horizon 2 (AWS adapters, LocalStack via env).
Publisher Lambda, CDK infrastructure, IAM roles (ApplicationRead/Publisher/Admin) — horizon 3.
React/MUI dashboard with schema-generated forms, diff preview, history, rollback — later horizon.
CI/CD examples and snapshot pinning — later horizon.
Metrics hooks (featuresync_* counters) — later horizon; never auto-sent telemetry.
Percentage rollout, analytics, experimentation, Redis, database, custom auth, multi-cloud — excluded from MVP by docs section 28.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The core is rule-heavy domain logic: flag definitions, typed configuration, targeting rules, immutable versioned snapshots and their validity invariants.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A named flag, either boolean or typed config, identified by a kebab-case key.
An immutable, versioned, validated set of all features for one environment.
A `when` condition over context attributes plus the value returned when it matches; first match wins.
The attributes (plan, country, platform…) passed to evaluate(), validated by a Zod schema.
A port that loads a raw snapshot from somewhere (file now, S3 later).
Replacing the active snapshot only after the new one fully validates, so readers see old-whole or new-whole.
The in-memory runtime object applications call: isEnabled/get/evaluate/version/has/getAll/ready.
The CI checks every change must pass: typecheck, lint with layer boundaries, 100% coverage tests.

phases.name: Set up the monorepo with quality gates
phases.goal: A pnpm TypeScript monorepo where every package is typechecked, linted with layer-boundary rules, and tested with a hard 100% coverage threshold in CI.
phases.rationale: The requirement is production-grade and fully covered code. Enforcing that mechanically from the first commit is far cheaper than retrofitting it; layer-boundary lint rules keep the DDD layering honest without relying on review.
changes: Create pnpm workspace with packages/* and a core package skeleton exporting from src/index.ts
Enable TypeScript strict plus noUncheckedIndexedAccess and exactOptionalPropertyTypes
Configure ESLint flat config with typescript-eslint type-aware rules and import/no-restricted-paths so src/domain imports nothing from application or infrastructure
Configure Vitest with v8 coverage and thresholds of 100 for lines, branches, functions, statements
Add CI workflow running install, typecheck, lint, test with coverage on push and PR
Add Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a README stating the local-first positioning
phases.expectedResult: `pnpm verify` runs typecheck, lint and tests with enforced 100% coverage, and the same command passes in GitHub Actions CI.

rubric.label: Gates fail on violations
rubric.ruleStatement: Each gate must turn red on a real violation, not merely exist.
passCriteria: A deliberately uncovered branch makes `pnpm verify` exit non-zero
A domain file importing from infrastructure fails lint
A type error fails typecheck
failureExamples: Coverage thresholds set but `--coverage` not passed in CI, so they never apply
no-restricted-paths zones written with wrong globs so nothing is ever flagged

rubric.label: Strict compiler settings
rubric.ruleStatement: Shared tsconfig enables strict and the unchecked-index/exact-optional flags for all packages.
passCriteria: packages extend tsconfig.base.json
No package overrides strict to false
failureExamples: Core tsconfig not extending the base, silently running non-strict

rubric.label: CI runs the same command as local
rubric.ruleStatement: CI invokes the identical verify script developers run locally.
passCriteria: ci.yml calls `pnpm verify`
Node version pinned via .nvmrc and used by CI
failureExamples: CI runs `vitest run` without coverage while local runs with it

phases.healerHint: Prove each gate by making it fail once on a throwaway violation before declaring the phase done.

phases.name: Model flags, rules and snapshots as domain types
phases.goal: Pure domain types and Zod contracts for Feature, Rule, Snapshot and Version, plus a typed defineFeature() helper.
phases.rationale: Every other part of FeatureSync (runtime, S3 sync, publisher Lambda, UI, CLI) reads or writes the same snapshot. Defining it once as a validated, immutable, language-neutral JSON contract is the DRY centre of the whole product.
changes: Define the snapshot JSON contract in Zod: schemaVersion, environment, version (positive int), createdAt, createdBy, previousVersion, reason, features map
Model boolean and config features; config features carry default value and ordered rules
Create Snapshot as a deeply frozen value object built only through a parse function returning a Result (ok or typed validation error)
Add defineFeature({ key, schema, default, context? }) that validates the default against the schema at definition time and infers config/context TypeScript types
Validate that every rule value in a snapshot conforms to its feature's registered schema when definitions are supplied
inputs: docs/notes-01.md context schema and type-safe API
phases.expectedResult: A `parseSnapshot()` function that turns unknown JSON into an immutable typed Snapshot or a descriptive validation error, with defineFeature() providing inferred types.

rubric.label: Snapshot contract is language-neutral JSON
rubric.ruleStatement: The persisted snapshot contains only JSON data; no Zod or TS-specific constructs leak into it.
passCriteria: Snapshot fixtures round-trip through JSON.stringify/parse unchanged
schemaVersion field present and validated
failureExamples: Storing serialized Zod schemas inside the snapshot
Using Date objects that serialize differently than they parse

rubric.label: Snapshots are immutable
rubric.ruleStatement: A parsed Snapshot cannot be mutated at any depth.
passCriteria: Test proves nested config mutation throws or is impossible by type and at runtime
failureExamples: Object.freeze on the top level only, leaving rules arrays mutable

rubric.label: Validation errors name the path
rubric.ruleStatement: Invalid snapshots produce errors naming the feature key and field path.
passCriteria: Tests assert error paths like features.payment-flow.rules[0].value.maxAmount
failureExamples: Returning a generic 'invalid snapshot' string
Throwing raw ZodError from the public API

rubric.label: Domain has no I/O
rubric.ruleStatement: Domain files import only zod and sibling domain files.
passCriteria: Lint boundary rule passes
No fs, process.env or clock access in src/domain (createdAt is data, not Date.now())
failureExamples: defineFeature reading process.env for the environment

rubric.label: Inferred types are tested
rubric.ruleStatement: Type inference from defineFeature is verified by type tests, not only runtime tests.
passCriteria: expectTypeOf or @ts-expect-error tests prove wrong config keys/enum values fail to compile
failureExamples: Types that silently widen to any, passing every runtime test

phases.healerHint: Keep the domain a set of pure parse/construct functions over plain data; freeze deeply and test types with expectTypeOf.

phases.name: Build the local rule evaluation engine
phases.goal: A pure, deterministic function that evaluates a feature against an evaluation context and returns the resolved value.
phases.rationale: Local evaluation is the product's core promise: no network call per flag check. Rule semantics must be exact and fully specified because future SDKs in other languages must reproduce them from the same snapshot.
changes: Implement operators equals, notEquals, in; multiple keys in `when` combine with AND
Evaluate rules in order; first match returns its value, otherwise the feature default
A disabled feature returns disabled/default regardless of rules
Missing context attribute means the condition does not match (never throws)
Validate context against the feature's context schema when one is defined; invalid context returns the default and a typed reason
Return a result object { value, enabled, reason: 'RULE_MATCH' | 'DEFAULT' | 'DISABLED' | 'INVALID_CONTEXT', ruleIndex? }
Write docs/spec/evaluation-semantics.md as the cross-language contract with a shared JSON test-vector file
inputs: Snapshot and Feature types from snapshot-domain-model
phases.expectedResult: `evaluate(feature, context)` returns a deterministic EvaluationResult, verified against a shared JSON test-vector file that documents the semantics.

rubric.label: Every edge case is specified and tested
rubric.ruleStatement: Missing attributes, type mismatches, empty rules, disabled features and rule order each have a documented outcome and a test vector.
passCriteria: test-vectors.json covers each listed edge case
Spec doc and tests reference the same vectors
failureExamples: Comparing number 5 to string '5' with == so it matches in JS but not in a future Go SDK

rubric.label: Pure and deterministic
rubric.ruleStatement: Evaluation has no side effects, no I/O and no randomness.
passCriteria: Same inputs always give deep-equal output; property-based test with fast-check
failureExamples: Caching results in a module-level Map keyed by context object reference

rubric.label: Never throws at runtime
rubric.ruleStatement: Bad or partial context degrades to the default with a reason, never an exception.
passCriteria: Fuzz/property test with arbitrary context never throws
failureExamples: Calling .includes on an attribute that turned out to be undefined

rubric.label: Operators extendable without editing evaluate
rubric.ruleStatement: Operators live in a registry so new ones (later: percentage) are added without modifying the evaluation loop.
passCriteria: evaluate.ts has no switch on operator names
failureExamples: A growing if/else chain inside evaluate()

phases.healerHint: Write the JSON test vectors first, then make evaluate() pass them; keep operators as a small typed registry.

phases.name: Build the in-memory flag client with atomic swap
phases.goal: The public FeatureFlags client that holds the active snapshot in memory, answers flag queries synchronously, and replaces snapshots atomically through a SnapshotSource port.
phases.rationale: Applications need one small, predictable object to call. Keeping loading behind a port means the same client works with a local file now and S3/SNS later, with no change to application code.
changes: Define SnapshotSource port: load(): Promise<unknown> and optional subscribe(onChange) for push-based sources
Implement SnapshotStore holding one immutable Snapshot reference, replaced only after parseSnapshot succeeds
Implement createFeatureFlags({ source, definitions?, logger?, allowStaleStartup? }) with isEnabled, get, evaluate, version, has, getAll, ready, refresh, close
ready() resolves after first valid load and rejects on startup failure unless allowStaleStartup with an initial snapshot
On an invalid or failed refresh keep the previous snapshot active and report through the injected logger
Make query methods synchronous and generic over defineFeature types so keys and return types are checked at compile time
Never throw from query methods; unknown key returns the definition default or false
inputs: parseSnapshot and evaluate from previous phases
phases.expectedResult: `createFeatureFlags()` returns a client whose queries are synchronous in-memory lookups and whose refresh swaps snapshots atomically, keeping the old one on failure.

rubric.label: Old-whole or new-whole, never partial
rubric.ruleStatement: Readers never observe a partially applied snapshot, and failed refreshes leave the prior snapshot active.
passCriteria: Test: invalid second snapshot → version() still returns first version and logger received an error
Test: concurrent refreshes resolve to the latest valid version without interleaving
failureExamples: Assigning features into the existing map one by one while validating

rubric.label: No I/O on the query path
rubric.ruleStatement: isEnabled/get/evaluate are synchronous and never call the source.
passCriteria: Test with a spy source asserts load() count is unchanged after 1,000 queries
Methods return non-Promise values by type
failureExamples: Lazy-loading on first get() call

rubric.label: Depends only on ports
rubric.ruleStatement: The application layer depends on SnapshotSource and Logger interfaces, never on fs or AWS.
passCriteria: Lint boundary passes
All tests use in-memory fake sources
failureExamples: Default source that silently imports the file adapter

rubric.label: Startup failure behaviour matches the spec
rubric.ruleStatement: Startup without a valid snapshot fails ready(), unless allowStaleStartup is set with a fallback.
passCriteria: Tests for both modes
Error type is exported and documented
failureExamples: ready() resolving with an empty snapshot so every flag silently reads false

rubric.label: Small, documented public API
rubric.ruleStatement: index.ts exports only the client factory, defineFeature, ports, result and error types.
passCriteria: API surface snapshot test (e.g. exported names list) is checked in
TSDoc on every export
failureExamples: Exporting SnapshotStore internals for convenience in tests

phases.healerHint: Hold a single immutable reference and replace it in one assignment after validation; test with fake sources only.

phases.name: Load snapshots from a local JSON file
phases.goal: A SnapshotSource adapter that reads a snapshot from the path in FEATURESYNC_FILE, with optional file watching, proven end to end.
phases.rationale: Developers must be able to use FeatureSync with no AWS at all (docs section 8). This adapter also proves the port design and gives the first end-to-end usable release of @featuresync/core.
changes: Implement FileSnapshotSource reading and JSON-parsing a file path; read errors and malformed JSON surface as typed load errors
Add optional watch mode using fs.watch with debounce that triggers client refresh
Add createFeatureFlagsFromEnv() that reads FEATURESYNC_FILE and builds the client with the file source
Write an end-to-end test: temp file → ready() → evaluate() → rewrite with invalid JSON → old version kept → rewrite valid → new version active
Add examples/node-local showing defineFeature + evaluate, and document usage in the package README
phases.expectedResult: Setting FEATURESYNC_FILE and calling createFeatureFlagsFromEnv() yields a working client, proven by an end-to-end test using real temp files.
phases.compensation: Adapter is additive; revert the infrastructure folder and env factory export without touching domain or application code.

rubric.label: End-to-end on real files
rubric.ruleStatement: The e2e test uses real temp files and the public API only.
passCriteria: Test uses os.tmpdir, cleans up, imports only from the package entry
failureExamples: Mocking fs in the e2e test, so path and encoding bugs go unseen

rubric.label: Configuration only through env/options
rubric.ruleStatement: Environment variables are read only in config-from-env.ts; the adapter takes explicit options.
passCriteria: grep shows process.env only in config-from-env.ts
Missing FEATURESYNC_FILE yields a clear config error
failureExamples: FileSnapshotSource reading process.env internally, making it untestable in isolation

rubric.label: Watch mode survives bad writes
rubric.ruleStatement: Partial or invalid file writes during watch never replace the active snapshot and never crash the process.
passCriteria: Test writes truncated JSON during watch and asserts version unchanged
close() stops the watcher with no open handles
failureExamples: Unhandled rejection from a read racing with an editor's atomic-save rename

rubric.label: Example runs as documented
rubric.ruleStatement: examples/node-local runs with the README commands and prints evaluated values.
passCriteria: CI runs the example as a smoke test
failureExamples: Example importing from src paths that differ from the published entry

phases.healerHint: Keep env parsing in one tiny factory and prove the adapter with real temp files, including a truncated-write case.

successCriteria: An application can defineFeature() with a Zod schema, point FEATURESYNC_FILE at a snapshot, and call isEnabled/get/evaluate/version/has/getAll/ready with zero network I/O; invalid snapshots are rejected while the previous one stays active; CI enforces strict TS, lint layer boundaries and 100% coverage.
Set up the monorepo with quality gates: `pnpm verify` runs typecheck, lint and tests with enforced 100% coverage, and passes in GitHub Actions CI.
Model flags, rules and snapshots as domain types: parseSnapshot() turns unknown JSON into an immutable typed Snapshot or a descriptive validation error.
Build the local rule evaluation engine: evaluate(feature, context) is deterministic and verified against shared JSON test vectors.
Build the in-memory flag client with atomic swap: synchronous queries, atomic refresh, old snapshot kept on failure.
Load snapshots from a local JSON file: createFeatureFlagsFromEnv() works end to end on real files.
deferred: S3 snapshot source, SNS listener, periodic reconciliation — horizon 2; integration tests hit LocalStack purely via AWS SDK env config (AWS_ENDPOINT_URL etc.), no LocalStack code paths.
Publisher Lambda (validate, version, write snapshot, update current.json, publish SNS, audit metadata), CDK stack and least-privilege IAM roles — horizon 3.
@featuresync/nestjs module, DI, @FeatureFlag decorator, FeatureFlagGuard — later horizon.
featuresync CLI: init, validate, pull, snapshot (with --version pinning), publish, rollback — later horizon.
Dashboard (React/Vite/MUI): environments, feature list, schema-generated forms, rules UI, diff preview, version history, rollback — later horizon.
CI/CD examples (GitHub Actions, pinned snapshots, offline tests) — later horizon.
Metrics hooks (snapshot version/age, sync totals/errors, evaluation totals) exposed for user-wired OpenTelemetry/Prometheus; no automatic telemetry — later horizon.
Percentage rollout, analytics, experimentation, Redis, database, custom auth, multi-cloud, extra SDKs — excluded from MVP by docs section 28.
